utterances.text: And if I've asked this question before, I apologise, and I think I have, but can you give us any idea which ethnicities, when we're talking about paramilitaries, which ethnicities the members were concerned with? Were they concerned with Serb paramilitaries, Croat paramilitaries, Bosniak paramilitaries, what?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I think all paramilitaries were of concern to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I jumped ahead a little bit, and I had you talk about some events that happened after the ARK Crisis Staff was formed. What I'd like to do now is go back and have you tell us your recollection of the events leading up to the ARK Crisis Staff. And I'd like to show you again an exhibit you've already looked at, and that is Exhibit 168 from the Prosecutor. That is the decision of 5 May 1992 signed by the president, Mr. Erceg.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: You remember this document from our earlier conversations. Correct?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting. This document is dated 5 May 1992. When did you first become aware of this document?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I first became aware of it the next day after the session was held.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: And in your job duties and in the time you spent there, did you become aware of why the Crisis Staff was formed? Was there a specific event or events that prompted it?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: No, no, I really don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I want you to look under paragraph 1, it lists the 15 people -- I want you to look at the first 15 individuals.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Do you know where did these 15 individuals come from? Were they -- do you know which municipality they came from?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: They're all from Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Look at number 16: Did the order, the decision, if you will, did it provide for any individuals from other municipalities to be part of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Not at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. Doesn't paragraph or entry number 16 deal with the -- the English translation is "presidents of municipalities"?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Well, read paragraph 16. What does it say? Entry number 16; it's not paragraph number 16.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't have the B/C/S version. Yes. Item 16, it says: "Presidents of Crisis Staffs of the Municipality" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead. Sorry for interrupting you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Item 16 says: "Presidents of the Crisis Staffs of Municipalities." It must be abbreviated. They probably mean municipalities. And item 17, I don't know what it means. I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. It would appear that the majority of the members are from Banja Luka. Do you know why on this regional body most of the people came from Banja Luka? Do you have any idea?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Fair enough. During this time, in the early part of May 1992, did you have any conversations with Mr. Kupresanin about your working with the ARK Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. He told me the day after it was established that some sort of Crisis Staff was established for the region. And he said the president of the government, that is, the prime minister of the Serbian Republic, Mr. Dzeric, would probably not like it because he had only issued instructions for Crisis Staffs to be created on the level of municipalities, and he speculated this decision would cause an even greater conflict among municipalities, or rather between municipalities on the one hand and the government of the Republika Srpska and the region on the other hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: All right. And did he give you any advice as to whether or not you should go work, continue to work with the ARK in this form, that is, the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did. He told me "be there, see what people want you to do. Otherwise you'll be out of a job." That's what he said. Because for all practical purposes, the Assembly of the Autonomous Region was not operating.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Were you given any specific tasks other than what you have just described for the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Specifically, were you ever tasked, were you ever asked to be responsible for the taking of the minutes or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: No, I was never responsible for the minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Would that have been a job, a responsibility of yours as the secretary to the assembly?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It would have been precisely my responsibility. But in order for minutes to be drawn up, some record has to be taken or recordings have to be made in order for the minutes to accurately reflect the discussion. An audiorecording would be required for proper minutes to be made.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I understand that you didn't take the minutes. But I take it -- well, let me ask it so it's a nonleading question. Did you attend meetings of the ARK Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I did. We did.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I know you didn't take the minutes, but did you ever take any rough notes, any personal notes to try to capture --

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: My job was only to take note of what everyone -- what every individual was suggesting as a conclusion. Usually after one item has been discussed, everyone would suggest a conclusion or their version of a conclusion, because there were many people present. At the outset, there were not so many. But later on, deputies arrived from the territory of Krajina, and the total rose to 30.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. I just want to try to have you tell the Chamber that while you attended these meetings, did you keep any handwritten notes, anything like that?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: After we would arrive at some conclusion, they would be typed out. There was no strict rule, no strict procedure according to which the session was held. People talked in turn, sometimes interrupted each other. And there was no strict procedure wherein we would have an agenda and then go from item to item. When you analyse the conclusions, you can see that there was no systematic agenda.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: We'll come to that in a minute. Here's my question. I know you didn't take the minutes. You told us that. I'm wondering if you wrote down anything during these meetings. If you did so, whether there's any of those documents still in existence today.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: No, no. Under the item "draft conclusion," which would take up one page, we would write our suggestions.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: How long did you hold on to any personal notes or personal handwritings? Did you hold on to them for any period of time or did you throw them away? What did you do with them?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I didn't hold on to them at all. As soon as the conclusions were typed out on a typewriter, I threw the drafts away. I didn't hold on to them at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I want to talk with you -- who ultimately became the president of the ARK Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Brdjanin, through this decision signed by Mr. Erceg.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: And I want to talk to you about your knowledge if any about how he became president. And you had indicated to me that this is something you wanted to discuss in private session. I'm bringing this up only as a courtesy to you because of what you told me. If you want to discuss it in private session, which means it is not being broadcast, that is something we can bring up with the President of the Chamber. So as a courtesy to you, I'm bringing that point up now.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: It's all the same to me. You don't have to do it in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, I just wanted to make sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's okay. You can still play the requiem later on in the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: What was Mr. Kupresanin's position with the ARK region?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kupresanin was the president or the speaker of the Assembly of the Autonomous Region at that time. Mr. Brdjanin was then vice-president. And there was also Mr. Knezevic from Drvar who was copresident. So Mr. Brdjanin was one vice-president, and Mr. Knezevic was another vice-president.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Did Mr. Kupresanin have any interest in becoming the president of the ARK Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: No, he didn't. As I said, he was a sickly man. And as a result of his previous outspokenness in the assembly, he was not very popular with the army or the police because he constantly criticised their work. But he was reluctant to clash directly with Mr. Dzeric. And he quoted that as the reason for not taking over the presidency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. How do you know this and he quoted it to whom? Did you ever have a tete-a-tete discussion with him? Did you discuss this with him? How come you know that he was reluctant? How do you know this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was a matter of discussion at one of the sessions of the Crisis Staff when the deputies asked why Mr. Kupresanin as president of the assembly was not ex officio president of the Crisis Staff, and that was the explanation he gave at one of the sessions of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes, Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Did Mr. Kupresanin ever give you any other reason besides his health and what you've just stated about why he didn't want to be president of the Crisis Staff? Did he ever make any statements about the competence, if any, of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did. He said: "Why should I assume responsibility for one body if the government left it to municipalities to appoint and replace directors of enterprises and all the other positions?" The government of Republika Srpska appointed directors of enterprises of republican importance, and it was stipulated that the directors and other appointees of the government, including municipal authorities, are accountable to the bodies that appointed them. And that is one of the reasons why he didn't take over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Who came up with the suggestion or the nomination of -- who came up with the suggestion that it should be Radoslav Brdjanin, president of the ARK Crisis Staff? Who nominated him, or who appointed him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I don't know. I wasn't there when the Crisis Staff was set up. The Crisis Staff of Krajina. I didn't attend that session. I started attending only when sessions had been underway for a while. I didn't know -- I didn't know anything about that time when Mr. Erceg set up the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You never came to know who appointed Radoslav Brdjanin as president of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No, I didn't. I never found out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I'd like to have the witness to have available P168, which is the listing of the members of the Crisis Staff because I'm going to ask him some questions about specific members.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could we have it on the ELMO, please, as well. Maybe Ms. Gustin has an extra copy that we could temporarily make use of.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I've got a clean copy right here, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Sir, you just told us just a minute ago, and I'm quoting: "I started only attending when the sessions had been underway for a while." What does that mean? What's your recollection of when you started attending?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: No, no. You didn't understand me. It's not that I arrived at sessions late. It's that I didn't attend the founding session where the members were elected, so I don't know anything about that session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Were the members elected or were they appointed? Because I don't think -- this is the first time I'm hearing that the members of the ARK Crisis Staff were elected. Are you sure they were elected and not appointed by the Executive Council of the Autonomous Region of Krajina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, they were appointed. I misspoke. Nobody elected them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Just to make it clear, yes. Yes, Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I also wanted to follow up on something you said earlier. I think you said that the Crisis Staff presidents were not there at first. Could you clarify what you meant by that.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: At first, I didn't attend. At the beginning, the composition is as it says here. And then after a few sessions, they started arriving; that is, the deputies and presidents of various municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: As they started arriving, did any of the members on this list, P168, stop attending?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: The majority of them stopped attending. They attended a few times. I don't know how many times they attended. However, later on, they stopped attending.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Judge, may I point out a possible mistake in the transcription. Page 67, line 1, the witness says "at first, I didn't attend."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: And I think it should be "they," referring to the Crisis Staff presidents, municipal Crisis Staff presidents didn't attend. So if I could ask him a question to clarify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: When you -- I want to just clarify. Did the Crisis Staff -- municipal Crisis Staff presidents attend at first?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: No. At first, they didn't attend.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I think that's clear now. And you were at all the subsequent meetings after the Crisis Staff was appointed. I want to talk to you, based on your recollection - and I realise it has been several years - do you know how many times Mr. Radic attended?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember. He may have attended once or twice, but I can't remember exactly how many times he attended. It was certainly not more than two times.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: And did he, Mr. Radic, ever express his attitude towards the competence of the ARK Crisis Staff to you? Did you ever hear him talking about that?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He said immediately that this body does not have any foundation, and that municipalities work on the basis of the instructions of the work of the Crisis Staff which was issued by the president of the government, Mr. Dzeric.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Just so it's clear, when you say that the municipalities work on the basis of the instructions of the work of the Crisis Staff, are you referring to a municipal Crisis Staff or a regional Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Municipal Crisis Staffs.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Radic was a member of the ARK Crisis Staff. You tell us he could not have attended more than two times. You told us about his attitude about the ARK Crisis Staff. Was he ever sanctioned or punished or penalised for failing to attend?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: No, nobody suffered any consequences for not attending.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I want you to look at P168 because I'm going to ask you similar questions for everyone there, from number 2 to number 15. Number 2, the individual reflected there, what is your recollection as to the number of times he attended?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: If my memory serves me right, he may have attended a few times.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: When you say "a few," is that a majority of the time, meaning more than half of the meetings? Or do you have any recollection?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Fair enough. What about the individual reflected in number 3, Mr. Kupresanin? How often did he attend?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: He attended very often.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. You've told us his - Mr. Kupresanin's - attitude towards the Crisis Staff and its competence over the time that the Crisis Staff was in existence. Did his attitude ever change, "his" being Mr. Kupresanin's?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: He perceived this body as a body which rallied around itself, deputies from Bosanska Krajina. A body which was supposed devise the strategy that the deputies from Krajina will adopt at the sessions of the Assembly of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. What about the gentleman reflected in number 4? Did he attended often?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: No, not that often. At that time, he was the president of the executive council of the region. And this body was very busy. He himself was in charge of various funds, the retirement fund, the health fund, the education, healthcare. All of these services were funded from the funds of the executive council of the region. There was a law on tax on the sales of goods and services which was adopted by the national assembly. All of these monies were paid into the funds in the region of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: And I appreciate that information at the end, but remember to keep your answers focussed to the question that I ask. I'm not criticising you, but please try to do that. It will easier for everyone involved. You say -- your answer when I asked you "did he attend often," you say no, he didn't attend that often. I appreciate that, but it doesn't give the Chamber an idea of how often that is. Does it attend half the time, a third of the time? If you can quantify it, at all, could you please try to do that, sir.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Maybe one-third of the time. But I can't be sure of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. Were you aware of Mr. Erceg ever being sanctioned or penalised for not attending the meeting of the ARK Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: No, nobody suffered any consequences for nonattendance.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: The next name on the list, number 6, is Dr. Vukic. How often did he attend, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: What about the gentleman at number 7, Dr. Milanovic? Did he attend all the time, some of the time, none of the time? What is your recollection?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember. Really, I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I'm going to skip number 8 and I'll come back to that because I want to spend a little time there. But the gentleman reflected at number 9, do you remember how often he attended?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: No, I can't. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Did there come a time when what I'll call the Banja Luka contingent, those individuals reflected here in 1 through 15, that they started attending less and less and less?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I believe so, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Cunningham, I mean, the way you phrased the question and the way it has been answered, which is no surprise to me, gets us nowhere because we were getting there bit by bit by reference to individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: And I still intend to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And if you stop halfway as you did, I don't think we can justify the conclusion of the witness, especially since we have left number 1 out. Anyway, let's go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. I'll get back on track following your instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: We left off with number 9. Let's talk about the individual reflected in number 10. Did he attend every meeting? What is your recollection of his attendance record, sir?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You don't remember how often Stojan Zupljanin attended?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: What about Mr. Kuzmanovic or Dr. Kuzmanovic?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I think that he resigned very soon afterwards, and he was replaced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, he is right. This document, in a way, is outdated, or was superceded by another one. But don't worry about it. We can get the name. There is the Gazette, 227, where we have the revised list.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you can supply the name, Ms. Korner --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's Dr. Mrdjanic, I believe. I'm just checking that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I believe you're correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's not important. Go to number 12, Milan Puvacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: What can you tell us about this gentleman's attendance at the ARK Crisis Staff meetings?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember that very clearly, but not that often.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: All right. The gentleman reflected at number 13.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Jovo Rosic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The same goes for him. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. What about number 14?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Slobodan Dubocanin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember either.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Finally, number 15, what's your recollection there?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember how many times he attended.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So you don't remember anything about 10, 11 we still have to say, 12, 13, 14, 15. You haven't been asked on number 8. You don't remember much about 9. You haven't told us about number 1. That's Radoslav Brdjanin. You know very little about Sajic. Erceg you gave us an approximation. Radic, you were quite firm about. And Kupresanin the same. So what makes you so firm in your mind to answer Mr. Cunningham's question suggesting that at a certain time the representation of -- or the attendance of the Banja Luka group dwindled to nothing, or almost? What makes you come to that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have said a moment ago. Later on, it was mostly delegates from the Bosnian Krajina that made up the sessions, and the executive council members, because they discussed topics of republican importance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes, Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Let's go and talk about the two names, the two numbers we left out. The first one is the accused, Mr. Brdjanin. Was he there every meeting? What's your recollection?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I think he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. Let's talk now about number 8, General Talic. How many times did you remember him attending?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember him attending except once. I know that once delegates from Krajina, representatives of municipalities, demanded from General Talic that the May issue, the May generation of soldiers who were sent to serve in the army be not sent to Herzegovina or the area of Mount Romanija, but rather be kept within barracks within the territory of Bosnian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. We'll talk about that in a minute. But what I'd like for you to do is look at P227, that is the ARK Gazette, and go to the entry for May 22 -- excuse me, 22 May 1992. And I want you to look at entry number 4 under the conclusions. I want you to read that to yourself. And when you're done reading, let us know so I can ask you a question. Are you ready? Why -- do you know why this conclusion, number 4, was issued?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, the coordination between the army and the Crisis Staff was very, very poor. In view of the law on the army and the division within the army where you know exactly who is answerable to whom, for instance corps commanders are accountable to the Ministry of Defence or the General Staff, they report to them, et cetera, et cetera. There was absolutely no coordination between this Crisis Staff and the army. There were several instances in which army tried to mobilise delegates to the assembly, although assemblymen were exempt from military service. In other words, the cooperation and coordination between civilian authorities and military authorities was indeed very poor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cunningham, I'm full aware of which conclusion you are questioning the witness about. But -- leave it, usher. Leave it. But I'm also pretty sure that conclusion number 4 that we see on the ELMO now is not the conclusion that you are questioning him about.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, Judge, I didn't even look.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Have a look at it now. Let's find the right one. At least we owe it to the public who may be following the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's page 26.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Tenancy rights.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I know which one you're questioning him about, but the public wouldn't be able to understand what you're talking about and what he is talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Now, if I might continue, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: It says here "mandatory attendance is requested." By him, Mr. General Talic, or his designee. Following this conclusion did General Talic attend ARK Crisis Staff meetings beyond the one instance that you recall?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: No. He sent a representative of the corps who was in charge of civilian affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Was that -- what role did that individual - I think it's a Colonel Vujinovic - what role if any did he have with the ARK Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I think his role to convey everything that was said at sessions of the Crisis Staff to his superiors.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: You mentioned earlier that there was an instance where there were questions for General Talic related to I believe you said some conscripts. Do you remember mentioning that earlier?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Earlier on when you were asked whether you recall Mr. Talic -- General Talic ever attending meetings of the ARK Crisis Staff. You said yes, I remember once, one occasion --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's the only thing I recall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And you referred to the topic that was discussed on that occasion about the allocation, also your relocation of soldiers within a specific area. I think Mr. Cunningham wants to question you about that debate.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I'd like to refer to P227, entry number 11. In the English version it's page 20. It's the conclusions 15 May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Specifically, sir, I'll direct your attention under those conclusions to conclusion number 5.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Having read that, are these the talks that you were -- that you referred to earlier?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: And do you know whether or not these talks ever took place?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know. I don't know whether he complied with the demands of the people who sent him this. I really have no knowledge of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Let's break it down. When you say "he," I take it you're referring to General Talic?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: When you talk about the demands of the people, tell us as best as you can what you're referring to. What are the demands?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, the demands of the people who attended a session of the Crisis Staff and who asked him to do this.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: And so you don't know the result, if any, of these talks. Correct?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Earlier on, you had told us that -- you had mentioned that the ARK Crisis Staff did not have any procedures. What I'd like for you to do now is to paint a picture, if you will, describe for the Chamber what a typical meeting was like. First of all, did anyone control the meetings? Was there a chairman, a person who led the discussions or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Brdjanin was the chairperson. But it was not exactly the rules of procedure of that body. People asked for the floor, suggested topics, and whatever the person who got the floor wanted to say, they would say. And they would raise whatever issues they saw fit. There was no agenda.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues]... If I could have the interpreter say something --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you hear us now? Can you hear the interpreter now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can you hear the interpreter now, Mr. Cunningham?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I can't hear anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I suggest you change your headphones.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: If I could have the interpreter say something.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, can you hear us now? It's channel 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I'm on channel 4. Still a -- can I borrow those. No, it's just there's a lot of static in this one now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you want, you can actually also move to where Mr. Ackerman was standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Let me see how this works, Judge. And if not, I'll just slide over.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Is it better now? Can you hear the English channel now?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I can hear it loud and clear. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: You say that there was no agenda. How would the subject of discussion -- how would they be decided?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, the participants would ask for the floor and suggest a subject of debate. They would say: "I am not happy with the situation in this or that area, and I would like to say a few words about it."

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: And who would be the individual who would recognise the speaker so they could take the floor?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: When the meetings ended -- after the meetings ended, would the representatives be mailed a copy of the agenda, the proposed agenda, for the next meeting?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: No, no. They would come to an agreement immediately when they would meet again. They would agree on that at the end of each session.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: And then when they would meet at the --

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: It is common knowledge that there were frequent power cuts at that time. Communications did not work. So they couldn't count on that. They would set a date immediately for the next meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Did any of the representatives from the municipalities ever have difficulty in getting to Banja Luka for Crisis Staff meetings?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know if they had any problems or not. At that time, problems were very common. There was a shortage of fuel and a shortage of all staples. But the main problem was transport.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. We know from looking at the Gazette that there were a number of decisions and conclusions issued by the ARK Crisis Staff. Was there a voting procedure in determining whether a conclusion should be adopted, if that's the word?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: No. No, there wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: The very last area that I want to talk to you, and I think we can get it done in the limited time that we have, is -- deals with the physical plant of the ARK Crisis Staff. And by that, I mean the offices. First of all, where did the ARK Crisis Staff meet at?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: The Autonomous Region of Krajina's Assembly -- or the Autonomous Region of Krajina as an authority did not have its own premises. The assembly also met in the offices of other bodies, because they had none of their own. And the sessions of this Crisis Staff were also held in the municipal building of Banja Luka in a hall that could seat from 30 to 40 people. 30, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: When it was held in borrowed office space, what was it like? Was it crowded? Did everyone have a place to sit? What was it like?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I don't think, Your Honour, he said that the Crisis Staff met anywhere else. He's talked about the assembly meeting elsewhere, but not the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right, Ms. Korner. Ms. Korner is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Let me see if I can clarify that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Did the ARK Crisis Staff ever meet in any offices?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Outside the municipal building, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: No, I mean in any offices.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you are asking in any offices, that, he has answered. Where did the Crisis Staff -- the ARK Crisis Staff meet? Not the Assembly of the Autonomous Region of Krajina, but the ARK Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Crisis Staff met in the building of the municipality of Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Always there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, always there.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Final questions, and I think I can get this done in two minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: If you can look at, again, Exhibit P227, which is the ARK Gazette, go to entry number 15. On the English version, that's page 26, and specifically looking at entry number 1 under the conclusions. Sir, that conclusion says: "By 30 May 1992, the second floor of the employment bureau building is to be fully prepared to house the offices of the ARK." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Did that ever come to fruition? Meaning did the ARK -- any part of the ARK ever move into that office space on the second floor?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, what is the ARK? Do you mean the Crisis Staff, the Assembly?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Did any entity associated with the Autonomous Region of Krajina move into the second floor of the employment bureau building as reflected in this conclusion?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: No. No, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Do you know why that is?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I think that the medical faculty occupied those premises at the time. And a lot of funds would have had to be invested in the required renovation and adaptation to the purposes of the assembly of the autonomous region.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm at a perfect breaking point if this is where we're going to break for the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Cunningham. I thank you, Mr. Blagojevic, as well. We haven't finished as you know, as you see. We will continue tomorrow at 9.00 in the morning. And I better advise you that it's very unlikely that we finish tomorrow. So we'll probably go -- I'm pretty certain that we will go into Friday. And I hope that we will finish by Friday.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I just mention because of course the witness hasn't finished his evidence in chief, we will give Your Honours later on today or Your Honours' secretaries a potential list of exhibits, but it may be added depending on what he says tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, I appreciate that, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I just wanted to notify the Chamber as well as Ms. Korner, I think I'll finish right around the first session tomorrow. I think I'll be done around the first break or just passed that. So I'm right on schedule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's fine, Mr. Cunningham. I'm still pretty sure that we won't finish tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I don't know whether Your Honour's reading my mind or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anyway, Mr. Blagojevic, the usher will attend to you. He will escort you out of the courtroom. Have a nice evening, and we will meet again tomorrow morning. Thank you. Anything else before we adjourn? Good. We stand adjourned until tomorrow morning at 9.00 in this courtroom. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 30th day of October, 2003, at 9.00 a.m. 25
